summary: Automated payment hold triggered by forecasted usage spike due to delayed metering writes
description:
Issue summary:
Textory Labs reported that their account was placed on an automated payment hold and received an overage forecast notification on 2026-02-20 despite actual token/embedding consumption remaining within expected limits for the billing period.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: API keys were temporarily suspended for new requests for ~3 hours while the payment hold was in effect.
- Billing: An overage forecast email and automated hold were triggered; no final invoice had been issued.
- Operational: Customer could not perform model deployments that require billing in good standing.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated tenant for Textory Labs (dedicated pool).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Affected services: billing-forecast service, metering-worker, alerting pipeline.

Steps to reproduce / Observed behaviour:
1) Textory ran a scheduled nightly batch for embeddings between 03:00-03:20 UTC.
2) Metering-worker that aggregates batch usage failed to push deltas to billing datastore due to a transient DB timeout; retries were delayed by backoff configuration.
3) Forecasting service ran with stale historical data (missing the previous day's write) and projected a sudden spike based on partial rates, marking the account as likely to exceed committed usage.
4) Automated billing policy applied a temporary payment hold and triggered an overage forecast email to the billing contacts.

Expected behaviour:
- Metering writes should be durable and retry within SLA so forecasting uses accurate data. Forecast service should avoid hard holds on single-run anomalies when data freshness is degraded.

Logs / Evidence:
- Metering-worker logs (attached): metering-worker-2026-02-20-03:05.log -> DB timeout + exponential backoff entries.
- Forecasting run: forecast-run-2026-02-20-03:30 shows delta spike compared to windowed baseline.
- Billing action log entry: billing-policy-action-2026-02-20-03:45 -> automated_hold: true.
- Slack thread: #support (link below).

Attachments: meter-logs (s3://redwood-support/textory/metering-2026-02-20.tgz), forecast-run JSON snapshot.
comments: 2026-02-20 03:55 - Maya Patel (Support): Acknowledged from Textory. They report keys blocked and urgent request to remove hold. Escalating to billing and metering teams. Slack: #support @here link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345/p1640

2026-02-20 04:12 - Diego Ruiz (Billing): Investigating billing action, pulling policy logs. Found automated_hold triggered by forecast-run id=fr-20260220-0315. Pausing any auto-enforcement while we validate data freshness. (INT-4121)

2026-02-20 05:02 - Priya Nair (Metering Eng): Found metering-worker encountered repeated DB timeouts during 03:01-03:18 and retries were spaced beyond expected window due to backoff config. Opened PR to tighten retry jitter: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering-worker/pull/148

2026-02-20 06:30 - Support (to customer): We temporarily lifted the hold at 06:15 UTC to restore API access while we complete root cause analysis. We will follow up with final resolution and any billing adjustments.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Missing metering writes caused forecasting to extrapolate a larger spike from earlier partial deltas.

Query run: SELECT sum(tokens) FROM billing.delta WHERE account_id='textory' AND event_date BETWEEN '2026-02-19' AND '2026-02-20'; Query showed gap for date '2026-02-20' in the hourly partition (partition write failures).
Observed: Metering-worker logs show repeated SQLState=57014 timeouts to billing-db-primary. Retries used exponential backoff configured to 30s,60s,120s which pushed final write past forecast window.

Forecasting service does not currently check 'freshness' signal before enforcing hold; it trusts latest available window. Proposed short-term mitigation: add freshness threshold and 'do not enforce' flag when upstream writes are older than 2 hours.
Related config: billing-policy config 'auto_hold_on_forecast' set to true for dedicated accounts above enterprise threshold. Consider toggling for post-migration test customers.
resolution:
Temporary: Support removed the automated hold at 2026-02-20T06:15Z and restored API access. Permanent: Metering-worker retry behavior updated (PR merged: metering-worker/pull/148) to ensure writes complete within 10 minutes under transient DB issues. Forecasting service was patched to require data freshness >90 minutes before auto-enforcement; patch merged and rolled out 2026-02-27 (billing-service/pull/879).

Billing action: No invoice had been issued, so no charge reversal required. We issued a customer note and applied a goodwill credit of $450 for the outage window and escalated a follow-up to the account team.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Metering team (Priya Nair): monitor retry success rates for 2 weeks.
- Billing/Forecast team (Diego Ruiz): add unit tests for freshness gating and add an alert if forecasting run sees >20% difference between windowed baseline and current with missing partitions.
- CS/Account (Maya Patel): confirm customer acceptance of credit and close the loop.

All changes validated in staging and rolled to prod by 2026-02-27. Issue closed.
